story_description: Implement stdin/stdout JSON-RPC communication between Blaze and Codex CLI app-server process
task: Implement Diff Computation from Before/After Content
task_description: Create CodexDiffComputer to compute unified diff hunks from Codex item/fileChange before/after content pairs
atom_description: Implement line-by-line diff algorithm that takes before (original) and after (modified) file content strings and produces FileDiff with hunks array compatible with DiffViewer and FilesSidebarView
problem_statement: Codex CLI item/fileChange events provide full before and after file content but Blaze FileDiffProduced events require unified diff format with hunks containing line additions, deletions, and context. Need an algorithm to compute the diff from raw content pairs without relying on external tools like git diff.
scope_in: Line-by-line diff computation from before/after string content
DiffLine generation with type (context/addition/deletion) and line numbers
Edge case handling for new files (empty before) and deleted files (empty after)
Async computation wrapper for large file performance
scope_out: Binary file diff support (text only for MVP)
Git integration or external diff tool invocation
assumptions: Before/after content are UTF-8 encoded strings
Line endings are normalized (LF or CRLF handled consistently)
Files under 100KB do not require chunked processing
Context lines default to 3 lines above and below changes (standard unified diff)
constraints: Must produce DiffHunk format compatible with existing DiffViewer.swift
Algorithm must be pure Swift with no external dependencies
Computation must be async to avoid blocking main thread on large files
Output hunks must be contiguous (no overlapping line ranges)
functional_requirements: FR1: Accept before String, after String, and path String as input parameters
FR2: Split content into lines and compute longest common subsequence (LCS) or Myers diff
FR3: Generate DiffLine entries with correct type (context, addition, deletion) and line numbers
FR4: Group consecutive changes into DiffHunk objects with accurate oldStart/oldCount/newStart/newCount
FR5: Add configurable context lines (default 3) around each change group
FR6: Return FileDiff object with computed hunks and file path
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Diff computation for typical files (under 1000 lines) must complete in under 100ms
NFR2: Memory usage must be linear O(n+m) where n and m are line counts
NFR3: Algorithm must handle files up to 100KB without timeout
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create CodexDiffComputer struct with static async compute method signature
Step 2: Implement line splitting with consistent newline handling (split on LF, trim trailing CR)
Step 3: Implement Myers diff algorithm or simplified LCS to find edit script
Step 4: Create edit script to DiffLine converter that tracks old and new line numbers
Step 5: Implement hunk grouper that merges adjacent changes within context distance
Step 6: Add context line padding to each hunk (3 lines default)
Step 7: Construct FileDiff with computed hunks and return
Step 8: Add empty before handling (all additions) and empty after handling (all deletions)
data_model_changes: No new data models - uses existing DiffHunk, DiffLine, DiffLineType, FileDiff from Models.swift
api_contracts: CodexDiffComputer.compute(before: String, after: String, path: String, contextLines: Int = 3) async -> FileDiff
ui_states: N/A - this atom is engine-layer computation; UI consumes FileDiff via DiffViewer
ui_interactions: N/A - no direct UI interaction; computed diff renders in existing DiffViewer
ui_copy: N/A - no user-facing strings; errors handled by caller
edge_cases: EC1: Empty before content (new file) - all lines are additions with oldStart=0, oldCount=0
EC2: Empty after content (deleted file) - all lines are deletions with newStart=0, newCount=0
EC3: Identical before and after - return empty hunks array
EC4: Single line change in large file - generate minimal hunk with context
EC5: All lines changed - single hunk spanning entire file
EC6: Binary content detection - check for null bytes and return error or placeholder diff
EC7: Very long lines (over 10KB) - truncate for display but preserve for diffing
failure_modes: FM1: Memory exhaustion on huge files - add file size guard with error return
FM2: Timeout on pathological diff cases - add iteration limit in Myers algorithm
FM3: Encoding errors in content - handle as replacement characters and continue
rollback_plan: Revert to stub implementation that creates single hunk with all lines as additions until algorithm issues resolved

Test empty after produces all-deletion hunk for deleted file
Test identical content produces empty hunks
Test single line insertion generates correct hunk metadata
Test single line deletion generates correct hunk metadata
Test multi-hunk generation for scattered changes
Test context lines correctly pad hunks
Test line number tracking for old and new files
integration: Test CodexEventMapper uses CodexDiffComputer for item/fileChange events
Test computed FileDiff renders correctly in DiffViewer
Test FilesSidebarView displays correct addition/deletion counts from computed stats
ui: N/A - computation layer with no UI components
perf: Memory profile to verify O(n+m) allocation
security: Verify no path traversal possible through path parameter (path is metadata only)

completed_evidence: Green test suite for CodexDiffComputerTests plus manual verification showing Codex file changes in DiffViewer with correct highlighting
dependencies: Requires CodexEventMapper (T012) to call compute method; uses existing DiffHunk/DiffLine models from Models.swift
status_reason: Ready to implement after CodexEventMapper provides item/fileChange events
source_refs: Codex CLI item/fileChange event format with before/after content
open_questions: Should we use Myers diff or simpler LCS algorithm for MVP?
Do we need to handle mixed line endings (CRLF vs LF) in same file?
Should binary file detection use null-byte heuristic or content-type header from Codex?
notes: Myers diff algorithm is optimal O(nd) where d is edit distance. For MVP, simpler O(nm) LCS may suffice since most file changes are small. Codex before/after provides complete content so no incremental diffing needed.

risks: Myers algorithm may be complex to implement correctly in Swift
Pathological cases (many small scattered changes) may produce excessive hunks
Large file diffs may block UI if async not implemented correctly
mitigations: Start with simpler LCS algorithm and optimize to Myers if perf needed
Add hunk merging for adjacent changes within context window
Use Task.detached or actor isolation to ensure non-blocking computation
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to Codex file change display - Claude and Gemini adapters unaffected; DiffViewer still works with other diff sources
risk_register.fallback_plan: Return single hunk with all-additions as stub until proper diff algorithm implemented

events: Input: item/fileChange JSON-RPC notification from Codex with before/after content
Output: FileDiffProduced normalized event with computed hunks array
apis: Internal edit script computation and hunk grouping methods
state: Stateless computation - no persistent state between calls
Thread-safe: pure function with no shared mutable state
persistence: No persistence - computed diff stored via SessionStore as part of FileDiffProduced event
